title: Which location settings a sublocation has of its own and which it takes from the parent

prose.text: "Does this sublocation have its own firewall, authentication or XFF setting?" has a different answer for each setting.

prose.label: Firewall is where the sources disagree.
prose.text: {{console-sublocation-firewall-toggles}} The console and the API disagree on whether a sublocation has its own firewall flag {{divergence:sublocation-firewall-and-ips}}, and whether that flag is stored, ignored or inherited is open {{gap:sublocation-firewall-source}}. Firewall enablement and rule behavior per location are in [[zia.firewall]].

Whether a new sublocation inherits the parent's auth, firewall or SSL settings is open {{gap:inherit-everything}}. See [[zia.locations.sublocations]]. Surrogate IP and per-location authentication are covered in [[zia.authentication.surrogate-ip]] and [[zia.authentication.location-enforcement]].

checks.do: Whether the setting is parent-only in the API, and what the console shows for it, before assuming a sublocation has its own value.
Each setting on a new sublocation against its parent, since whether most settings are inherited is open.

parent-only-fields.statement: The OpenAPI schema marks `ofwEnabled` (Enable Firewall), `ipsControl`, `xffForwardEnabled`, `ports`, `vpnCredentials`, `ipv6Enabled` and `ipv6Dns64Prefix` as applying to top-level locations only. For a sublocation `xffForwardEnabled` is read-only and inherited from the parent.

expect.description:
Enable XFF Forwarding for a location. When set to true, traffic is passed to Zscaler Cloud via the X-Forwarded-For (XFF) header.

Note: For sub-locations, this attribute is a read-only field as the value is inherited from the parent location.

shared-fields.statement: The schema applies `authRequired`, `aupEnabled`, `cautionEnabled`, `surrogateIP`, `upBandwidth`, `dnBandwidth`, `profile` and `ipAddresses` to both parent locations and sublocations.

surrogate-not-inherited.statement: A sublocation does not inherit its parent's IP Surrogate setting; it is configured on the sublocation separately, and its Idle Time to Disassociation and known-browser options are set there.

quotes: Enable IP Surrogate: If you enabled Enforce Authentication, select this option if you want to map users to device IP addresses. Any sublocations associated with this location do not inherit this setting.
Enable IP Surrogate: If you enabled Enforce Authentication, select this option if you want to map users to device IP addresses for a sublocation.
In Idle Time to Disassociation, specify how long after a completed transaction the service retains the IP address-to-user mapping.
If you want to use the existing IP address-to-user mapping (acquired from the surrogate IP) to authenticate users sending traffic from known browsers, enable Enforce Surrogate IP for Known Browsers.

sublocation-auth-per-sublocation.statement: Enforce Authentication is a per-sublocation setting, which is what lets a corporate sublocation authenticate while a guest sublocation under the same tunnel does not.

quotes: Enforce authentication on the internal corporate network, while disabling it for the guest network.
Enforce Authentication: Enable to require users from this location to authenticate to the service.

console-sublocation-firewall-toggles.statement: The Add Sublocation window offers Enforce Firewall Control and Enable IPS Control among its Gateway Options.

quotes: Enforce Firewall Control: Select to enable the service's firewall controls.
Enable IPS Control: If you enabled Enforce Firewall Control, select to enable the service's IPS controls.

sublocation-firewall-and-ips.summary: The console presents firewall and IPS enablement as sublocation settings, while the API schema limits them to top-level locations.

quotes: Enforce Firewall Control: Select to enable the service's firewall controls.

positions.says: Enforce Firewall Control and Enable IPS Control are set in the Add Sublocation window.
`ofwEnabled` is marked as applying to top-level locations only (TOP).

sublocation-firewall-and-ips.impact: An agent or script that sets `ofwEnabled` on a sublocation through the API may be writing a value that is ignored or overridden, and a legacy note that sublocations carry their own firewall flag is not safe to repeat.

inherit-everything.title: Whether a new sublocation starts from the parent's settings
inherit-everything.detail: Unverified legacy statement: "A newly created sublocation does not automatically pick up the parent's auth, firewall, or SSL settings" and "A newly created sublocation does not inherit the parent's `auth_required`, `ofw_enabled`, `ssl_scan_enabled`, or other toggles. Each sublocation must be explicitly configured." Only IP Surrogate is documented as not inherited (surrogate-not-inherited); `xffForwardEnabled` is documented as inherited, and `ofwEnabled` is parent-only in the schema. Resolve by creating a sublocation through the API and comparing it to its parent.

sublocation-firewall-source.title: Where a sublocation's firewall enablement comes from
sublocation-firewall-source.detail: The schema marks `ofwEnabled` and `ipsControl` as parent-only while the console offers both on a sublocation (see the divergence). Whether the sublocation's value is stored, ignored, or inherited, and which one the firewall rules honor for sublocation traffic, is not stated. Resolve by reading a sublocation's `ofwEnabled` after changing the parent and the sublocation in turn.
sublocation-firewall-source.blocks: stating whether a location-scoped firewall rule can reach a sublocation's traffic
